title: Kotlin Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: main is the starting function. println prints a value on a new line.
notes: A program needs a main function to start here.

entries.name: Keep a fixed value
entries.summary: val gives a name to a value that cannot be reassigned.
notes: Use var only if the binding must change.

entries.name: Update a variable
entries.summary: var lets you assign a new value. += adds to the current number.
notes: A variable keeps its type even when its value changes.

entries.name: Build a message
entries.summary: A dollar sign places a variable value inside a Kotlin string.
notes: Use ${...} for an expression, not just $.

entries.name: Choose a value
entries.summary: if can return a value. Both branches below produce a message.
notes: An if used as a value needs an else branch.

entries.name: Read a list
entries.summary: listOf makes a read-only list. The first item has index zero.
notes: Use a mutable list when you need add or remove operations.

entries.name: Count with a range
entries.summary: The range 1..3 includes both ends. for reads each number.

entries.name: Write a short function
entries.summary: A function gives steps a name. This expression body returns n times two.
notes: Write a type for each function input.

entries.name: Handle no value
entries.summary: A question mark makes a type nullable. ?: supplies a fallback for null.
notes: The !! operator can crash when the value is null.

entries.name: Read safely
entries.summary: ?. only calls a property or method when the value is not null.
notes: A safe call may return null, so handle that result too.

entries.name: Keep related data
entries.summary: A data class stores fields and supplies useful data operations such as copy.
notes: copy makes a new value; it does not change the original.

entries.name: Match a choice
entries.summary: when picks a branch for a value. else handles the values not listed.
notes: A when used as a value must cover every possibility.
